concept.title: Inline Formatting
concept.abstract: This section covers Inline Formatting in HTML — the inline formatting attributes that assign semantic meaning to individual words or phrases within a paragraph — and five scenarios: bold for general emphasis, bold for a UI element inside a procedure, monospace for inline code, monospace for a file path, and bold for a menu navigation sequence. The converter reads each named character style or font family to determine the appropriate DITA inline element; where named styles are absent, content pattern recognition refines the mapping.

conbody.p: Inline Formattingare attributes applied to individual words or phrases within a paragraph. For example,

ul.li: A menu path or button label is bold to identify UI screen text as a named interface element.
A file path or command is monospace to identify it as executable or navigable content.

conbody.p: Marking these distinctions visually — bold, italic, or monospace — communicates meaning to readers. Translation memory tools, conditional processing engines, content reuse frameworks, and accessibility processors all require typed markup to treat each kind of text correctly in publishing systems.

The HTML-to-DITA converter evaluates each recognized HTML inline element within its surrounding paragraph and maps it to the appropriate DITA inline element. General emphasis is preserved using <b> or <i>, while recognized patterns within <code> or <span> elements are converted to more specific DITA elements such as <codeph>, <filepath>, <varname>, <cmdname>, or <menucascade>. This semantic mapping preserves the meaning of inline content while keeping the surrounding paragraph intact.

conbody.note: Use semantic inline elements to identify emphasis, user interface controls, commands, code, file paths, variables, and menu navigation. Avoid using inline formatting solely for visual presentation, as unrecognized or non-semantic markup may be converted to plain text, reducing the semantic value of the generated DITA output.
